# DD-003: The Query Lexer

**Scope.** The `tdb-lexer` crate turns text into tokens for all four models
(Redis-style key-value, relational/ORM, vector, graph). It does not parse: it
never decides what a statement means, only what its words are. A parser comes
next and consumes this token stream.

**Implementation.** The scanner is generated by [`logos`](https://docs.rs/logos)
from two token enums (`crates/tdb-lexer/src/raw.rs`): one for normal mode and
one for KV mode. `lexer.rs` turns their output into the public `Token`s, adds
line/column positions, and handles statements. Anything the DFA cannot express
(escapes, doubled quotes, error positions) is a small callback.

## Choosing the model

Two entry points:

- `Lexer::new(input)` **detects** each statement's model from its first word
  (the rest of this section's first half). Every keyword is recognized, and one
  input may mix models. For tools that read scripts.
- `Lexer::for_model(input, model)` **fixes** the model. This is what a router
  that already knows it from the connection (`/keyval/<db>`, `/rdbms/<db>`,
  `/vector/<db>`, `/graph/<db>`, DD-004) should use. There is no detection, and
  only that model's keywords are reserved:

| Model | Lexed as | Keywords |
|---|---|---|
| `Keyval` | Redis-style, one command per line, for every statement | the KV commands |
| `Rdbms` | normal mode, runs through `;` | shared + relational + `VECTOR` |
| `Vector` | normal mode, runs through `;` (SQL-like for now) | shared + relational + `VECTOR` |
| `Graph` | normal mode, runs through `;` | shared + graph |

So `MATCH` is an ordinary name under `Rdbms`, and `SELECT` is an ordinary name
under `Graph`. `Keyword::in_model(model)` says which words a model reserves. The
`Keyval` dialect has no comments at all, and a line whose first word is not a
KV command still lexes (as a `Word`); rejecting it is the parser's job.
`Model` uses the route names: `Keyval`, `Rdbms`, `Vector`, `Graph`.

## Why one lexer needs modes

The four syntaxes conflict at the character level:

| Text | Redis wants | Cypher wants |
|---|---|---|
| `user:1` | one key | `user` `:` `1` |
| `a-b` | one key | `a` `-` `b` |
| `http://x` | one value | `http` `:` `/` `/` `x` |

So the lexer decides **per statement**. Before the first token of a statement it
reads one word; if that word is a Redis command, the statement is lexed in **KV
mode**, otherwise in **normal mode**.

- A statement starts at the beginning of the input, after a `;` (normal mode),
  and after the newline that ends a KV statement.
- The word is the longest run of `[A-Za-z0-9_]`. The statement is KV mode when
  that word is a KV command (see below, case-insensitive) **and** the next
  character is whitespace or the end of the input. `GET(` is not a KV command.
- Whitespace (newlines included) and `//` / `/* */` comments before the first
  token are skipped, so blank lines and comments may separate statements.

## Normal mode (relational, vector, graph)

Whitespace, including newlines, separates tokens. Statements end at `;`.

**Words.** `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`. A keyword (case-insensitive) becomes
`Keyword(k)`; anything else is an `Identifier`. The token `value` keeps the
original spelling (`select` stays `select`). `` `any text` `` is an `Identifier`
whose value is the text inside; a doubled backtick is one backtick. This is how
a keyword (or a name with spaces) is used as a name. An empty `` `` `` is an
error.

**Numbers.** Unsigned. `Integer` is digits. `Float` has a fraction
(`3.14`), an exponent (`1e3`, `2.5E+10`, `1e-3`), or both. A `.` or `e` that is
not followed by digits is not part of the number: `1.` is `Integer(1)` `Dot`,
`1..3` is `Integer(1)` `DotDot` `Integer(3)`, `1e` is an error. A letter or `_`
directly after a number is an error (`12abc`). There is no leading-dot form
(`.5` is `Dot` `Integer(5)`). A sign is a separate `Minus`/`Plus` token.

**Strings.** `'...'` or `"..."`; both are strings (identifiers use backticks).
Inside, a backslash escapes `n` `r` `t` `0` `\` `"` `'`, and a doubled quote
character is one quote (`'it''s'`). Any other escape is an error. Strings may
contain newlines. The token value is the unescaped text.

**Parameters.** `$` then `[A-Za-z0-9_]+`: `$1`, `$name`. The value is what
follows the `$`. A bare `$` is an error.

**Comments.** `// to end of line` and `/* block */` (not nested). SQL's `--` is
**not** a comment, because Cypher uses `--` for an undirected edge; it is two
`Minus` tokens.

**Punctuation and operators**, longest match first:

| Text | Token | | Text | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<=>` | `CosineDistance` | | `(` `)` | `LParen` `RParen` |
| `<->` | `L2Distance` | | `[` `]` | `LBracket` `RBracket` |
| `<#>` | `InnerProduct` | | `{` `}` | `LBrace` `RBrace` |
| `<=` | `LtEq` | | `,` | `Comma` |
| `<>` `!=` | `NotEq` | | `:` | `Colon` |
| `<-` | `LeftArrow` | | `;` | `Semicolon` |
| `->` | `Arrow` | | `.` | `Dot` |
| `>=` | `GtEq` | | `..` | `DotDot` |
| `<` `>` `=` | `Lt` `Gt` `Eq` | | `\|` | `Pipe` |
| `+` `-` `*` `/` `%` | `Plus` `Minus` `Star` `Slash` `Percent` | | | |

Consequences worth knowing: `a<-1` lexes as `a` `LeftArrow` `1` (write
`a < -1`); `-->` is `Minus` `Arrow`; `<--` is `LeftArrow` `Minus`; a lone `!` is
an error. Any other character is an error.

## KV mode (Redis-style)

The statement is one command followed by arguments, ending at the **end of the
line**. A `;` does not end it (it is just a character).

- The first token is the command: `Keyword(k)`.
- Each argument is separated by spaces or tabs and is one of:
  - a **quoted string** (`"..."` or `'...'`, same escapes as normal mode). The
    character right after the closing quote must be whitespace, a newline, or
    the end of the input;
  - a **bare word**: a run of non-whitespace characters, classified as
    `Integer` (`-?digits`), `Float` (`-?` number with a fraction or exponent),
    or else `Word`. So `user:1`, `a-b`, `10.0.0.1`, `http://x`, `-inf`, `(5`,
    `1.2.3`, `+5` and `1e` are all `Word`; `42` and `-5` are `Integer`; `3.5`,
    `-0.25` and `1e3` are `Float`. The `value` is the text as written.
- The newline that ends the statement is a `Newline` token (value `"\n"`);
  `\r` before it counts as whitespace. A final statement without a newline
  ends at the end of the input with no `Newline`.
- No comments in KV mode: `//` and `#` are ordinary word characters.
- Blank lines between statements produce no tokens.

**KV commands** (each starts a KV statement): `SET GET DEL EXISTS INCR DECR
INCRBY DECRBY APPEND STRLEN MGET MSET HSET HGET HDEL HEXISTS HGETALL HKEYS HVALS
HLEN SADD SREM SISMEMBER SMEMBERS SCARD LPUSH RPUSH LPOP RPOP LLEN LRANGE ZADD
ZREM ZSCORE ZRANGE ZRANGEBYSCORE ZCARD EXPIRE TTL PERSIST MULTI EXEC DISCARD`.
`SET` has no single home model (it is also `UPDATE .. SET` and Cypher's `SET`):
`Keyword::model()` is `None` for it, but at the start of a statement it is the
Redis command. Everywhere else a KV keyword such as `GET` is just a keyword.

## Keywords

Case-insensitive, canonical spelling upper-case. `Keyword::model()` gives the
home model, `None` when shared.

- **Shared**: `SET CREATE DELETE WHERE ORDER BY LIMIT AS AND OR NOT IN IS NULL
  TRUE FALSE ASC DESC`
- **Rdbms**: `TABLE DROP INSERT INTO VALUES SELECT FROM UPDATE OFFSET PRIMARY KEY
  INDEX ON` and the types `BOOL INT32 INT64 FLOAT32 FLOAT64 TEXT BYTES`
- **Vector**: `VECTOR`
- **Graph**: `MATCH RETURN DETACH MERGE SKIP`
- **Keyval**: the commands listed above (except `SET`)

Reserved words cannot be plain names; quote them with backticks.

## Positions

`line` and `column` are 1-based and count characters (not bytes); a tab is one
column. A token's position is its first character. For a string it is the
opening quote; for `EndOfFile` it is the position after the last character. A
`Newline` token sits at the newline character itself.

## Errors

All are `LexError { message, line, column }`, displayed as `message at L:C`.

| Message | Position |
|---|---|
| `unexpected character 'X'` | the character |
| `unterminated string` | the opening quote |
| `unterminated comment` | the `/*` |
| `unterminated quoted name` | the opening backtick |
| `empty quoted name` | the opening backtick |
| `expected a parameter name after '$'` | the `$` |
| `invalid escape '\q'` | the backslash |
| `invalid number '12a'` (number text plus the offending character) | the number's start |
| `expected whitespace after a quoted argument` (KV mode) | the offending character |

The lexer never panics, on any input, and a long input never exhausts the stack
(see "Details the tests pin").

## Details the tests pin

- Punctuation and operator tokens have their source text as `value`; an
  `EndOfFile` has an empty value.
- Whitespace is anything Unicode calls White_Space (so `\r`, `\u{a0}`,
  `\u{2028}` separate tokens). A lone `\r` is whitespace, not a line break; only
  `\n` counts a line.
- A quoted KV argument may span lines (`GET "a\nb"` is one argument), because
  the statement ends at the first newline *outside* a quoted argument.
- A run of characters of any length (a word, a run of whitespace, a `//`
  comment) is lexed in constant stack. The regex engine behind the lexer
  recurses once per character over multi-byte text when it is not optimized (a
  debug build), so these runs are matched by a short pattern plus a loop, and a
  test lexes 200,000-character runs. Statements come from the network, so this
  is about not letting a peer abort the server.
- `::`, `||`, `**`, `++` and `;;` are not tokens; they split into their
  single-character tokens.
- For a number followed by a letter, the message shows the number text plus that
  one character: `12abc` is `invalid number '12a'`, `1e` is `'1e'`, `1.5e` is
  `'1.5e'`, `1e3x` is `'1e3x'`, `1_000` is `'1_'`, `0x1F` is `'0x'`.
- Four backticks in a row are one quoted name whose text is a single backtick.
- `Display` of `Model`, `Keyword` and `TokenType` is the variant name, with
  keywords as `Keyword(SELECT)`.

## Not in scope

Parsing; `\xHH` / `\u` escapes; hex or binary numbers; `::` casts; `||`; nested
block comments; statement-level error recovery (the first error stops lexing).

## Rejected alternatives

- **One context-free token set**: forces Redis keys to be quoted, which Redis
  users will not accept.
- **Only a lexer per model, chosen by the caller**: right for a router (so it
  is now `Lexer::for_model`), but it cannot lex a script that mixes models,
  which is why detection (`Lexer::new`) stays.
- **A hand-written scanner**: it was the first implementation, and the `logos`
  one was checked against it on 900,000 generated inputs (identical tokens,
  errors and positions) before it was removed. `logos` makes keywords and
  operators declarative; the hand-written one was about twice the code.
- **Keywords as plain identifiers**: simpler lexer, but every consumer then
  re-implements keyword matching and the model of a statement is not
  discoverable from tokens.
